title: Lesson 9: Apple Silicon & Unified Memory Architecture — js-tools
desc: The SoC against a traditional motherboard, big.LITTLE cores, and Unified Memory Architecture where CPU and GPU share one RAM pool with no copy step — plus the two architectural prices UMA pays: bandwidth is shared rather than additive, and sharing memory requires cache coherency. Verified by running a hand-written engine: a 4K frame is exactly 33,177,600 bytes, PCIe Gen 4 takes 1.0368 ms against UMA's 0.0829 ms (exactly 12.5x, matching the bandwidth ratio), and with the CPU consuming 200 GB/s the same frame takes 0.1659 ms, exactly 2.00x slower. Demo: compare PCIe against UMA transfer time interactively.
